answer.headline: SFO leads the equal-weights screen of primary hubs
answer.body:
The equal_weights expansion screen covers airports stored as FAA hub class L, M, or S. The result is a screening rank of expansion opportunity, not a valuation. SFO {F1573} is ordered first. The next scores are BNA {F1575}, JAC {F1576}, BZN {F1577}, and ORD {F1578}. The screen marks BNA, JAC, BZN, and ORD as tied with the airport ranked immediately above. The score gap from SFO {F1573} down to ORD {F1578} is {F1760}. AUS {F1579} is the next airport. The screen does not mark AUS as tied with ORD, and the score gap from ORD {F1578} down to AUS {F1579} is {F1759}.

The top quartile of scored airports is the equal_weights order from SFO through SLC {F1609}. PHX {F1610} is the next airport. The screen marks PHX as tied with SLC, and the score gap from SLC {F1609} down to PHX {F1610} is {F1758}.

Seat factor in that set over {F1751.period} is P10 {F1751}, P25 {F1752}, P50 {F1753}, P75 {F1754}, and P90 {F1755}. The interquartile range is {F1756}. The span from P10 to P90 is {F1757}. Each airport counts equally.

The share of SFO operating hours above its verified instrument capacity rate is {F1574}. The screen flags SFO for instrument-condition headroom rather than a binding airfield constraint. Carrier-concentration flags in the top-quartile set, over {F1161.period}, are BNA {F1161}, EWR {F1188}, MIA {F1235}, IAD {F1206}, SJC {F1278}, OAK {F1242}, IAH {F1207}, DFW {F1182}, and SLC {F1279}. The SNA row carries a regulatory-cap flag for a verified passenger cap and commercial arrival and departure curfews. Concentration and the cap sit beside the rank. They are not inputs to the score.

claims.text: SFO {F1573} is ordered first on the equal_weights expansion screen of this primary-hub set. The next score is BNA {F1575}.

The following scores are JAC {F1576}, BZN {F1577}, and ORD {F1578}. The screen marks BNA, JAC, BZN, and ORD as tied with the airport ranked immediately above. The score gap from SFO {F1573} down to ORD {F1578} is {F1760}.
AUS {F1579} is the next score after ORD {F1578}. The screen does not mark AUS as tied with ORD. The score gap from ORD {F1578} down to AUS {F1579} is {F1759}.
SLC {F1609} ranks immediately ahead of PHX {F1610} on the equal_weights screen. The screen marks PHX as tied with SLC. The score gap from SLC {F1609} down to PHX {F1610} is {F1758}.

Over {F1751.period}, seat factor in the top-quartile set is P10 {F1751}, P25 {F1752}, P50 {F1753}, P75 {F1754}, and P90 {F1755}. The interquartile range is {F1756}. The span from P10 to P90 is {F1757}.
The share of SFO operating hours above its verified instrument capacity rate is {F1574}. The screen flags SFO for instrument-condition headroom rather than a binding airfield constraint.
Carrier-concentration flags in the top-quartile set over {F1161.period} are BNA {F1161}, EWR {F1188}, MIA {F1235}, IAD {F1206}, SJC {F1278}, OAK {F1242}, IAH {F1207}, DFW {F1182}, and SLC {F1279}.
The SNA row of this screen includes a regulatory-cap flag for a verified passenger cap and commercial arrival and departure curfews.

The seat-factor percentiles describe airport-level seat factor inside the equal_weights top quartile ending at SLC {F1609}. Each airport counts equally, so a small hub and a large hub have the same weight. These calculated ratios do not measure unmet demand, terminal capacity, fares, or profitability.

assumptions: Primary hubs means airports whose stored FAA hub class is L, M, or S: large, medium, and small hubs. Nonhub primary airports, hub class N, are excluded. The phrase did not resolve to a named place, so the analysis uses this hub-class group.
Hub class is the class stored on the airport record. It is not recomputed from enplanements inside this screen.

The top quartile is every scored airport with an equal_weights score at or above the upper quartile of the scored scores, using linear interpolation. That set is the screen order from SFO through SLC. SLC is on the cut and is included. PHX is the next airport and is below the cut. Airports the screen did not score are outside the set.
Seat factor is the catalog metric on the T12 window {F1751.period}. Each airport is weighted equally, not by passengers or by seats.
limitations: SJU, GUM, and STT are in the hub-class group and were not scored because home-CBSA per-capita income is missing. They have no screen rank and they are not in the seat-factor distribution.
No airport in the hub-class group was listed below the screen enplanement gate.

The screen marks long stretches of adjacent airports as tied, including the opening cluster through ORD and the boundary between SLC and PHX. A tie means the gap is inside the model tie band. The displayed order is still the score sort. The quartile set follows the percentile cut and does not expand along the whole tie chain.

Scored airports other than SFO are flagged AIRFIELD_UNKNOWN because no verified capacity rate is on file. No scored airport is flagged as airfield-binding. The SNA passenger cap and curfews are screen flags, not catalog metrics, so the cap levels are not reported here as findings.
This order is the equal_weights scenario. The same screen also returns base, demand_only, and momentum_heavy orders, and those orders differ.

The score does not measure costs, debt, airline-agreement economics, construction risk, unmet demand, terminal capacity, fares, or profitability. Its passenger-increase input is an unconstrained FAA forecast. Seat factor is passengers divided by seats on departing passenger and combi segments. It is not a capacity residual.
